plugins.name: mockup-fidelity
plugins.description: Validate that an implemented React or React Native UI faithfully reproduces a reference mockup (HTML+CSS, served prototype, Figma export, or another rendered component set), then update the code to close every gap — by measuring the rendered tree, never by eyeballing or reading source. Treats the mock as the source of truth, builds a COMPLETE screen/frame inventory (never silently drops a frame), extracts both sides to on-disk artifacts and generates the ledger from them, inverts the burden of proof (a visible difference is a defect until a citation proves it intentional), diffs structure-first then per-property computed styles, and produces a per-screen present/divergent/absent ledger plus a FUNCTIONAL-GAPS document for any newly-added UI that is only visual (missing backend, data wiring, endpoints). For React Native it measures the RENDERED tree — structural/accessibility extraction (axe describe-ui / Maestro hierarchy) plus resolved style props over the Metro CDP connection (rozenite / agent-cdp) — and forces every screen's measurement to disk as artifacts, so a 'match' verdict can never come from a screenshot, a source read, or reasoning (frontier vision models catch under half of fine-grained UI differences; an artifact-forcing gate plus a completeness-critic close that hole). For a React web target the comparison is symmetric DOM-to-DOM — reference and target are both read via getComputedStyle through one extractor at the same viewport, with the app chrome (sidebar/header/nav) in scope. Asks the user when unsure, on both a full-comparison and a per-screen basis. Generic and framework-agnostic — nothing app-specific. v2.6.0 re-platforms the capture harness onto Obscura over CDP (odiff-bin is now its only dependency): the element-scoped raster and IoU text-less layers stand, and the CDP rendered-font layer is recorded as available:false with its reason rather than as zero divergences, because Obscura loads no web fonts and every named family collapses onto one fallback face — confirm any typeface question in a real browser.
plugins._v251note: 2.5.1 adds a deterministic TYPOGRAPHIC-DECLARATION check (class font) to the single-script analyzer/differ (assets/diff/analyze.js), closing the 'same font, different declared SHAPING' class that slipped every layer on the diolog.site↔diolog.app run: a button rendered the SINGLE-story 'a' (Inter font-feature-settings:cv11) where live is normal (double-story), and elsewhere the font-family DECLARATION differed (target 'Inter', system-ui, …, sans-serif vs live Inter, sans-serif). BOTH slipped: the computed-style differ compares font-family only by KIND (serif/sans/mono) and never looks at font-feature-settings; CDP getPlatformFontsForNode reports the SAME font FILE because a cvXX glyph is a variant WITHIN the file; and the odiff raster runs antialiasing:true so a glyph-edge variant is suppressed as smoothing noise. Per PAIRED text element MODE B now runs three exact comparisons: (1) font/feature-settings — normalized getComputedStyle.fontFeatureSettings (lowercase, strip quotes, sort the comma list, collapse whitespace, ''→normal); (2) font/variation-settings — same treatment for fontVariationSettings (a wght/opsz axis applied on one side only); (3) font/family-exact — the FULL fontFamily declaration normalized, complementing (not replacing) the existing kind check. Because these props are almost always set site-wide, each is DEDUPED per (property|normalizedTarget|normalizedRef) to ONE root-cause finding + a [×N elements] count (a whole-site cv11 or stack difference = ONE finding, not hundreds). MED severity; same text-probe scoping as the other font checks. Validated against controlled fixtures via the real analyze.js MODE A→B flow: (a) cv11 vs normal fires 1 deduped finding; (b) long system stack vs Inter, sans-serif fires 1; (c) a font-variation-settings divergence fires; (d) identical pages = 0 new findings; (e) equivalent-but-different-syntax declarations (reordered/requoted) = 0 (normalization does not false-positive).
plugins._v25note: 2.5.0 adds the RASTER + CDP-rendered-font + IoU-text-less + systematic-pseudo layer. A new Node-side HARNESS (assets/diff/capture.mjs — playwright-core + odiff-bin) injects the unchanged analyze.js (MODE A reference / MODE B target) and ENRICHES its findings with three RENDERED signals a getComputedStyle dump structurally cannot give: (1) CDP RENDERED-FONT (CSS.getPlatformFontsForNode per visible text node — the genuinely-rendered familyName + isCustomFont; flags when live renders its loaded web font 'Inter Medium' while the target falls back to the system 'Helvetica' EVEN THOUGH getComputedStyle font-family lists Inter first on both — the trustworthy font-class signal, deduped per root cause); (2) ELEMENT-SCOPED RASTER DIFF (odiff on per-element crops of both full-page screenshots — a same-size box with a high pixel-diff and no other finding is a missing decorative child / occlusion / paint difference the DOM passes are blind to; size-mismatch raster diffs corroborate a geometry finding; 12% threshold + antialiasing to avoid text-edge flood); (3) IoU TEXT-LESS PAIRING (remaining bare svg/icon/decorative nodes paired by bbox Intersection-over-Union >= 0.9 so they too are presence/raster-checked). analyze.js itself gains SYSTEMATIC PSEUDO-ELEMENT extraction: capture() records pseudoStyle per node (::before/::after content, border-width/-color, background/-image, box-shadow, position, border-radius) and a MODE-B pass compares it for EVERY paired element (not just illustrations / not only the fold). Chromium launches with --font-render-hinting=none for deterministic raster crops (documented: this does NOT make headless == a real browser; the CDP rendered-font check, not any width or raster %, is the font-class authority). Findings carry bbox-delta + odiff mismatch% + rendered-font (the diff-as-instruction shape) + a summary.layers block. Deps: odiff-bin@4.3.8 + playwright-core@1.61.1 (prebuilt binaries, no node-gyp, reuse the host chromium cache); run npm install in assets/diff (and in any project's copied .mockup-fidelity).
plugins._v2note: 2.3.0 NARROWS the over-broad illustration-internal exclusion in the single-script analyzer/differ (assets/diff/analyze.js): a product ILLUSTRATION / mockup card (the ReadinessMockup 'Morrow Vale Resources' card, a hero product-shot, a readiness/preview panel) carries PLACEHOLDER content — fake tickers, demo numbers, sample labels — that legitimately differs, but its STYLING is real and checkable. Previously the differ dropped illustration internals ENTIRELY as noise, so real defects went unchecked (the card's row label had letter-spacing normal vs live's -0.3px, and the card had NO border vs live's 1px #e5e9f0 on ::after). Now MODE B SUPPRESSES only the placeholder TEXT-content comparison for illustration internals (a different demo ticker/number is not a finding → routed to noiseExcluded.illustrationInternals) while STILL comparing their COMPUTED STYLE — border (incl. the folded ::after/::before fold), border-radius, box-shadow, background/colour, letter-spacing, font-size/weight/family, padding, and geometry — pairing internals across sides BY POSITION/STRUCTURE (not text) and deduping repeated identical mockup-row styles to a few rows + a [×N] summary. 2.2.0 added the FONT-METRIC / VERSION detector (font/rendered-width-ratio — the SAME family at the SAME size rendering a consistently different width ⇒ a different font VERSION/metrics). 2.1.0 added the RENDERED-GLYPH-SHAPE / font-feature-effectiveness detector (font/feature-ineffective). 2.0.0 added INTERACTION STATES (:hover/:focus overrides from document.styleSheets) and RESPONSIVE (per-width 390/768/1280 desktop→mobile layout-TRANSITION divergence).

plugins.name: positioning-pipeline
plugins.description: End-to-end product-positioning pipeline. From a company context it generates two Google Gemini Deep Research prompts (a positioning brief + a product-research-persona market brief), renders a copy-and-launch HTML with animated Gemini instructions (select Deep research from the + menu; Share & Export → Copy contents), then — once the research comes back — synthesises three framework-grounded positioning territories (Ries & Trout, April Dunford, Blue Ocean, David C. Baker) as Markdown plus a stylised interactive decision page.

plugins.name: presentation-design-md-from-screenshots
plugins.description: Reverse-engineer a slide deck's visual design system from one or more slide screenshots and produce a single authoritative PRESENTATION_DESIGN.md — a tool-agnostic, token-based spec (canvas, palette, typography, slide archetypes, chart style, image treatment, iconography, motion, do/don't) hard-capped at 1,700 characters so another AI (Gamma, Beautiful.ai, Pitch, Keynote/PowerPoint co-pilots, Stitch, v0, Claude, Cursor) can generate new slides that unmistakably belong to the same deck. Sibling to design-md-from-screenshots but tuned for slides: fixed 16:9 canvas, slide archetypes, chart data-ink discipline, image treatment conventions, and on-slide positional grammar.

plugins.name: product-gap-analysis
plugins.description: Whole-product gap analysis for any project against any stated goal (v1.0, GA, a roadmap horizon, or the product's own stated intent) — 'where does this project stand and what's left?'. Surveys everything the repo has — status ledgers/orchestrator logs OR issue-tracker state, specs' deferral sections, untriaged briefs or roadmap docs, reference catalogues, the live app code, navigation/wiring, and the test inventory — via up to 7 parallel research agents (status-map, catalogue-currency, deferral-mining, backlog-classification, wiring-audit, test-coverage, product-coherence), adapting the lens plan to whatever artifact classes exist. Cross-checks every status claim against git (ledgers lie; git is authoritative), reconciles contradictions with a fixed authority order, and synthesizes one comprehensive evidence-cited gap report stratified into seven layers (coherence gaps ranked by contradiction-with-the-product's-own-claims, genuinely-unbuilt features, deferred tails + shared substrates, security/legal release gates + dark-by-default workers, test debt, docs drift, live defects) ending in a prioritized P0/P1/P2 proposed-work-items table that seeds the repo's pipeline (briefs or tickets). Read-only: writes one report, never product code. Built for reliable execution by Opus-class models — explicit agent prompt templates, epistemic laws, and a fixed report skeleton.

plugins.name: product-strategist
plugins.description: Generate validated, prioritized product feature concepts and outcome-based roadmaps for AI-assisted IR/compliance/governance SaaS. Supports feature ideation, roadmap construction, feature evaluation, data ingestion, and comparative prioritization using RICE-C/WSJF scoring, compliance gates, and OST methodology.

plugins.name: research-to-roadmap
plugins.description: Recursive deep-research pipeline with two tracks. Track R (product roadmap): grounds in the product's existing surface, authors strategic + high-volume-ideation + ~10 drill-down Gemini Deep Research prompts (exclusion blocks, analysis lenses, epistemic bounding), then synthesises the returned reports — via verdict ledgers, an evidence hierarchy, gates-track sequencing, and red-team discipline — into wave-based roadmaps with stable numbered, triage-ready feature entries. Track G (general): takes ANY topic, thought, or idea → one initial research prompt (via deep-research-prompt-creator) → pause for the user's Gemini run → 5–10 drill-down prompts from the returned report → pause → synthesis into a decision-ready document.

plugins.name: ship-feature
plugins.description: End-to-end feature delivery conductor for your product. Takes ONE feature (inline description or a markdown file) and drives it from a bare idea to merged, tested, production code by orchestrating the existing skills in a single in-session flow: design-craft (represent the whole feature UI in the design-system elements/composites/mock-pages, grounded in the repo's design system — e.g. apps/web-design-system — plus an optional DESIGN.md design-language spec when provided or present, and any provided HTML/CSS/JS mock) → triage (→ docs/specs/spec-DIO-XXXX.md) → plan (→ docs/plans/plan-DIO-XXXX.md) → work (implement in an isolated worktree) → a deferred-work loop (re-work, or child triage+plan+work for extra phases, all on the SAME branch) → gap-fix (close remaining spec gaps in code) → acceptance-e2e (a comprehensive e2e suite over every user flow/action/interaction/menu, run against the feature branch locally and fixed) → finalize (commit → rebase → merge into the integration branch → push → clean up worktree(s)). The conductor stays in-session so it keeps the accumulated feature context across every stage and leans on the on-disk spec/plan/mock artifacts as durable, resumable memory; parallelism lives inside each sub-skill's own Workflow fan-out. One feature = one branch = one worktree; the merge is behind a fail-closed pre-merge gate. Builds on the design-craft, feature-spec-pipeline (triage/plan/work/gap-fix), and acceptance-e2e plugins. v1.5 recalibrates the conductor for current-model behaviour (Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 prompting guidance): 'Verify, don't assume' becomes verify-with-oracles-not-by-re-reading (gates actually run, real paths exercised un-stubbed, out-of-family gates — but no separate pass whose only job is re-reading a stage's own output, which now costs tokens without adding recall), plus a front-load-the-whole-brief discipline (a complete spec handed over once and left to run is the condition the pipeline performs best under, which is what makes Phase 0's single question round load-bearing) and a report-thinly rule for narration and written artifacts. references/orchestration-model.md gains the effort column its model lane table never had, pointing at the new pipeline-wide canonical feature-spec-pipeline/skills/work/references/model-and-effort.md.

plugins.name: ship-fleet
plugins.description: Backlog-wide feature-delivery orchestrator. Surveys ALL remaining feature work in a product repo — LEDGER.md, docs/specs/spec-*.md, docs/plans/plan-*.md, untriaged briefs in docs/features-to-triage/, refined HTML mocks in design/mocks/html, deep research in docs/deep-research/ — reconciles any in-progress worktrees, then writes ORCHESTRATOR.md (a combined plan + ledger for everything left) and orchestrator-hierarchy.html (a visual dependency hierarchy) BEFORE any execution. It then drives the backlog to done by running the ship-feature skill per feature: dependency-ordered, up to 8 concurrent Opus runner agents, with mechanical plan-scoped coding optionally delegated to the Cursor CLI (composer-2.5) and verified/fixed by Opus, while the orchestrating session itself stays on the session model. Includes a preflight that checks the project's directory/file conventions (offering to clone diolog-team-files for CODING_PRACTICES.md / NEW_PROJECT_BEST_PRACTICES.md, gather stray feature briefs into docs/features-to-triage/, and validate the monolith layout against NEW_PROJECT_BEST_PRACTICES.md). Builds on the ship-feature plugin (and through it design-craft, feature-spec-pipeline, acceptance-e2e). Recalibrated for current-model behaviour (Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 prompting guidance + the effort docs): the runner wire self-check no longer hardcodes a dated model id (a check pinned to last generation's string fires WRONG-MODEL on every correctly-routed runner and stops the fleet before it starts — it now names the TIER, so a newer Opus passes and a wrong tier fails); launch rule 2 gains the effort dial (an agent spawned with no effort runs at `high`, `low` is the level built for subagents, a feature runner is the long-horizon shape `xhigh` exists for — pair it with `max_tokens` ≥64k — and a review lane should drop effort before model, since REVIEWER ≥ WRITER is about capability class); the warm/cold resume boundary is corrected from a ~5-minute prompt-cache TTL to the harness's current 1-hour TTL (~5 minutes only in usage overage), with the instruction not to design a pause strategy around one TTL; and Operating discipline gains report-thinly plus ORCHESTRATOR.md-is-state-not-prose. Per-lane effort is canonical in feature-spec-pipeline/skills/work/references/model-and-effort.md.

plugins.name: spec-validation
plugins.description: Validate whether a specification, build plan, or Definition of Done is GENUINELY implemented in a large codebase — not just rendered, schema-valid, and passing tests. Classifies every claimed-done data field as REAL (a producer computes it from the filesystem / git / discovery / AI / a live API), AUTHORED (read from persisted state but only ever written by a UI round-trip or a seed — nothing computes it), or MOCK (only ever a fallback constant), each with file:line evidence. Fans the work out across parallel investigators, adversarially verifies the highest-impact findings before reporting, and writes a ranked, date-stamped living gap report that doubles as the resolution backlog. Built to catch demo-data-dressed-as-done and to re-validate after a prior '100% complete' claim — the core insight being that renders + schema-valid + tests-pass never proves a real producer exists. Audit-only: it changes no product code — the gap-fix skill (feature-spec-pipeline) is the fixer.

plugins.name: token-discipline
plugins.description: Session-start operating defaults that cut token spend without cutting quality, tuned for Claude Opus 5. Targets where the tokens actually are — 96% of a session's bill is reused input, resent from the top every turn — so it addresses repetition, delegation and read width rather than prose length. Ships as a ~1029-byte literal designed to sit inside the cached system prefix, paid for once per cache window rather than re-read. Includes the reasoning for every rule, the four alternatives that were rejected as traps (tool-definition stripping, transport-layer prefix truncation, request-hash response caching, and a plain 'be concise' instruction), an explicit measured-vs-assumed split, and a comparison against prose-compression skills like caveman with the four-arm benchmark that would settle it. Perch injects this at session start behind a toggle; it also works standalone.

plugins.name: ux-craft
plugins.description: Book-grounded UX engine for implementing, mocking, and reviewing web and mobile UIs, layouts, and user flows, plus marketing and transactional emails. Operationalizes the UX canon — Krug (self-evidence, trunk test), Norman (affordances/signifiers/feedback), Garrett's five planes, Cooper's goal-directed design, Nielsen's heuristics, Wroblewski's mobile-first, Yablonski's Laws of UX, Weinschenk's behavioral science, Fogg/Cialdini/Eyal persuasion with a hard ethics gate, Tidwell patterns, Lidwell principles, Refactoring UI hierarchy tactics, Lean UX mock-to-learn — as three modes (Build / Review / Advise) over eight references: psychology-laws (research-cited mechanisms), review-playbook (multi-lens pass with severity honesty, intentional-vs-accidental deviation handling, evidence-format findings with pasteable fixes, and prompt-injection guards for reviewed content), flows-and-forms (GDS one-thing-per-page, validation timing, state machines, undo vs confirmation, wayfinding), mobile-ux (touch targets, thumb zones, iOS/Material platform grammar, RN notes), email-ux (two-second triage contract, client rendering constraints, transactional patterns, CAN-SPAM/GDPR compliance floor), ux-writing (microcopy patterns, tone matrix, Butterick typography), ai-product-ux (AI inputs/wayfinding/governors/narration/trust/tuners with friction-to-risk calibration and prompt-injection-aware retrieval rules), and per-surface pre-ship checklists incl. WCAG 2.2 quick pass and an AI-feature gate. The UX brain to design-craft's visual hands: it owns whether the thing works for humans; design-craft owns whether it looks intentional. v1.1.1 adds two pre-ship checklist floors routinely forgotten in mocks: designed not-found/error routes (no dead ends) and legally required links (privacy/terms/cookie consent). v1.2 adds a Working-posture section recalibrated for current-model behaviour (Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 prompting guidance): reviews run as two passes that must never be merged — find wide (every finding, including uncertain and low-severity ones) then filter hard (rank, merge, drop) — because a reviewer asked to be conservative reports less rather than better, and severity calibration is a filter-pass job; reports stay proportional to their findings rather than to the template, with empty sections dropped and no closing restatement; scope is held (review what was pointed at, raise a deeper problem in a sentence instead of auditing it uninvited); lens fan-out becomes the exception for scopes that genuinely exceed one pass, briefed content-first and questions-last, never spawned to grade its own findings, with the post-fix re-check scoped to regression on what changed; corrections are narrated only when they change the user's decisions; and every capture taken during a review must be opened, since a rendered screenshot nobody read is not evidence. ai-product-ux gains a Narration section treating the assistant's own words as a designed surface — progress-update shape, outcome-first closing turns, a threshold for narrating self-corrections, a caveat budget, voice specified by positive samples rather than prohibitions, and the verbose-is-not-transparent separation of trace depth from prose length — plus a narration-cadence line in the AI-feature pre-ship checklist and the matching question in the AI review lens.

plugins.name: workflow-resume
plugins.description: Find recent dynamic workflow runs that lost agents to API errors, and resume or finish them correctly. A workflow agent that hits a rate limit, usage limit, dropped connection or 5xx returns null with zero retries; parallel()/pipeline() map that to null too, the generated script's closing .filter(Boolean) drops it, and the run reports `completed` with the loss unreported. This skill separates the two shapes that need opposite handling: a finished run with dead agents, and a run that is still live (which must not be relaunched, and whose worktrees and pid-held locks must not be touched). Bundles a stdlib-only read-only scanner that reads the journal and per-agent transcripts rather than the snapshot, because a snapshot is written once at completion and is absent or stale for any live or resumed run; it reports run id, session id and whether that session is still alive, the scriptPath and args needed to resume, journal started/results counts, and each agent's item, state and error. Encodes the mechanics verified from the claude 2.1.220 bundle: the journal is filed under <SESSION-UUID>/subagents/workflows/<runId>/ so a changed session id cold-starts a resume silently (anthropics/claude-code#65796, open) and the fix is a cp -R relocation; the cache key is a sha256 chain over (previous key, prompt, normalised opts) with a sticky miss flag, so replay is a prefix and a run that failed early recovers almost nothing; and the /workflows `r` key only aborts a live AbortController, so a failed agent cannot be retried there. Also carries the reconciliation discipline that matters most in practice: cached results are what an agent said, not what landed, and runs have reported items merged whose branches were still tens of commits ahead of main, so branch ancestry and worktree state decide whether a failed item is resumed in place or re-run clean.

plugins.name: company-overview-from-website
plugins.description: Produce the company-overview markdown that the investor-portal generator reads: what a listed company does, who leads it, what it has lodged, and every image and PDF it publishes — crawled from the company's own site so every fact is attributable rather than authored.
